findings.title: Six writers of followerSlots; two hotfixes write via direct setFlag; createItem reactions unordered
findings.observed: follower-hooks (ActorEngine), FollowerSlotService, FollowerCreator (transaction), MinionCreator (direct setFlag), repeatable-entitlement hotfix (direct setFlag, own createItem/updateItem/deleteItem listeners) and orphan-transfer hotfix (direct setFlag) all read-modify-write the same array. Two createItem listeners react to the same talent without defined order; read-modify-write without a shared queue can lose updates.
findings.intendedOwnership: FollowerSlotService is the only writer; hooks and hotfixes call it.
findings.proposedSolution: Route every followerSlots write through FollowerSlotService (add the operations the hotfixes need: repair entitlements, transfer orphan); fold the repeatable-entitlement repair into follower-hooks reconciliation; then retire the two hotfixes. Extend tools/check-follower-mutation-authority.mjs to all writers and add it to CI.
findings.alternatives: Serialise writes per owner with the shell mutation queue.
findings.regressionTests: Concurrency test: two talents created back-to-back yield two slots; checker in CI.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: add/remove Attract Minion / recruiting talents repeatedly.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One slot writer; two hotfixes removed.

findings.title: Wrapper chains on combat and Force execution entry points
findings.observed: CombatOptionResolver.collectAttackModifiers is reassigned by 8 live modules and ForceExecutor.executeForcePower by 4; each wraps the previous value, so the effective behaviour is the composition in ES-module evaluation order, which no test pins.
findings.intendedOwnership: One resolver that iterates a declared contribution list (combat/force own the order).
findings.proposedSolution: Introduce explicit contributor registries (attack-modifier contributors; force-power post-execution steps) in combat/force and migrate each wrapper into a contributor with an explicit priority equal to its current effective order.
findings.regressionTests: Snapshot test of collectAttackModifiers output for a fixture actor with all relevant feats, before/after.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Attack rolls with stacked feat options; Force power execution.
findings.risk: High: attack math is a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: Store purchase rollback leaves CREATE-bucket droid/vehicle actors and reports rolledBack:true
findings.observed: executeMutationTransaction applies the merged plan non-transactionally (no transactional:true). ActorEngine applies CREATE (world actors) first; created-actor cleanup only runs when _txnSnapshot exists (transactional mode). On a later failure TE restores only the purchaser snapshot and returns rolledBack:true, so a purchased droid/vehicle world actor can remain without payment. Not covered by any test that injects a failure after CREATE.
findings.intendedOwnership: TransactionEngine guarantees the whole trade fails (OSI atomic trades).
findings.proposedSolution: In TE, track created actor ids (reuse ActorEngine tempIdMap via transactional:true, or a create-ids callback) and delete+verify them in the catch; report indeterminate unless cleanup is verified.
findings.alternatives: Create the asset actors only after the credit/ledger plan has committed (two-phase with compensating delete).
findings.regressionTests: Failure-injection test: store purchase with droid plan, fail ADD bucket; assert no orphan actor and outcome not rolledBack unless verified.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live checkout of a droid with forced failure.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One rollback implementation (ActorEngine transactional) instead of TE snapshot + separate cleanup.
findings.risk: Whole-actor restore semantics (TX-07b) if transactional:true is reused.

findings.title: createItem hook grants Starship Tactics maneuvers outside the progression shell; recursion guard key never set
findings.observed: On any feat named like 'starship tactics' created on the creating client, the hook opens a selection dialog and creates maneuver Items plus sets system.starshipManeuverSuite. The progression framework has its own starship-maneuver step and finalizer writes to starshipManeuverSuite. The hook's guard checks options.meta.guardKey==='starship-maneuver-grant' but grantManeuvers never passes it; createItem has no mutation-in-flight guard (updateActor does).
findings.intendedOwnership: A-15: maneuver choices live in progression draft state and are committed once by ProgressionFinalizer; non-progression feat grants route to a progression entry, not a hook dialog.
findings.proposedSolution: Restrict the hook to non-progression creations (skip when ActorEngine.isActorMutationInFlight or a progression source option is present) or remove it and launch the progression starship-maneuver step on out-of-progression grants. Pass the guard key from grantManeuvers.
findings.alternatives: Keep hook but convert to a notification prompting the player to open the progression shell.
findings.regressionTests: Test: finalizing chargen with Starship Tactics creates maneuvers exactly once and opens no dialog; adding the feat via sheet drop takes the approved path.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: chargen with Starship Tactics; level-up adding it; GM drop of the feat.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One maneuver grant path instead of two.
findings.risk: Progression finalization runtime-risk; duplicate grants possible.

findings.title: Mentor commitment decay runs on every client from an updateActor hook
findings.observed: The 'swse-mentor-decay' updateActor listener ignores userId, so every connected client that has previously observed the actor's level calls decayAllMentorCommitments, which setFlags the actor. Owners (GM + player) each apply the 15% decay (compounded); non-owners attempt a write they lack permission for. The per-client _actorLevelMap means the result depends on which clients were connected.
findings.intendedOwnership: Exactly one client (the originating user, or the active GM) performs advisory follow-up writes.
findings.proposedSolution: Guard with userId === game.user.id (or single active GM); better, perform decay inside the level-up finalization path (swse:level-up-complete is emitted locally by the finalizer) rather than an updateActor observer.
findings.alternatives: Compute decay lazily on read from stored levels instead of persisting decayed values.
findings.regressionTests: Hook test simulating two clients; assert one write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Two connected owners, level up once, check commitment value decayed once.

findings.title: Ungated deleteCombat cleanup and writes inside preUpdateActor
findings.observed: deleteCombat runs on every client; each loops combatants and issues unsetFlag/updateActor (non-owners error, caught for the whole loop). preUpdateActor awaits unsetFlag and a chat post while another update is in flight (Foundry does not await pre-hooks).
findings.intendedOwnership: Responsible-GM lifecycle service; no writes in pre-hooks.
findings.proposedSolution: Gate on isResponsibleGm(); move Crippling Strike cleanup to updateActor (post) with the same gate.
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: two users, one cleanup write.
findings.foundryAcceptance: End combat with two clients connected.

findings.title: Startup migrations gated on isGM, not the active GM
findings.observed: Every connected GM client runs autoLoad, abilityMeta repair and DSP migration at ready; the version setting is written after the loop, so two GMs loading together can both apply the migration. Compute is idempotent, so the likely effect is duplicate writes, not corruption - not verified.
findings.intendedOwnership: Exactly one client (game.users.activeGM) runs world migrations.
findings.proposedSolution: Gate on game.user === game.users.activeGM (as houserule-feat-grants canWriteGrants does) in a single migration runner.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test with two fake GM users.

findings.title: Light-sync hook writes token light on every client without gating
findings.observed: preUpdateItem runs on the initiating client only, but Hooks.once("updateItem") fires on the next updateItem of ANY item and then updates token documents; no GM/owner check seen in syncActorTokenLight. Token writes are Foundry scene documents (legitimate exception) but uncommented.
findings.intendedOwnership: one writer (active GM or owner)
findings.proposedSolution: Use updateItem with id match and an owner/active-GM gate.
findings.regressionTests: Hook fires only for matching item id.

findings.title: Lightsaber activation written outside the coordinator
findings.observed: Coordinator owns IGNITE_PATHS during ready-ignite; the item sheet / actor.activateItem write system.activated and emitLight separately. OA-12 keeps activation a separate fact, so this may be intended; not traced whether activateItem checks posture.
findings.intendedOwnership: OA-12 single readiness authority
findings.proposedSolution: Confirm with owner whether standalone ignite belongs to the coordinator; if yes route through an ignite intent.
findings.alternatives: Document as separate activation authority.
findings.regressionTests: Ignite while stowed is refused (if that is the policy).

findings.title: Location registry is a whole-array read-modify-write of one world setting
findings.observed: Every mutation reads the full registry, edits it and rewrites the setting. Library imports are serialized per client. The code itself states there is no cross-GM or cross-tab locking (:1050-1053). upsertLocation calls are not queued. Two concurrent writers (two GM tabs, or overlapping async calls) can lose updates.
findings.intendedOwnership: Single serialized writer.
findings.proposedSolution: Route every mutating method through the existing #importQueue pattern. Owner decides whether multi-GM editing is a supported scenario.
findings.alternatives: Store locations as world documents (JournalEntry or Items) instead of one setting.
findings.regressionTests: Concurrent upsert unit test.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Two GM tabs editing different locations.

findings.title: Settlement idempotency depends on the caller's session snapshot
findings.observed: settleSession checks escrow status on the session object passed in, pays, and only then persists 'settled'. TransactionEngine's per-actor in-flight lock covers only overlapping calls. A second settle using a stale snapshot after the first payout but before persistence would pay again. Pazaak has two settle call sites (completion and forfeit).
findings.proposedSolution: Re-read the session from GameSessionStore and persist a 'settling' claim before paying (the same pattern as the Party Fund V-P6C-20 settling claim).
findings.regressionTests: Concurrent settle unit test.

findings.title: Bonus Force Point pool: six builders, two flag scopes, outside the writer guard
findings.observed: Pool entries are normalized/built independently in ActorEngine, ForceExecutor (_normalizeBonusForcePointEntries, 351-token exact clone of GuardianSpiritActions._normalizeEntries), GuardianSpiritActions, force-adept, jedi-prestige and feats (buildBonusPool, 158-token clone of ForceExecutor). Five writers use the literal path flags.swse.bonusForcePoints; GuardianSpiritActions uses setFlag('swse') which SWSEActorBase redirects to flags[foundryvtt-swse], and getFlag('swse') prefers that copy, so after a Guardian Spirit write all ActorEngine debits and other grants become invisible (see F-TAL-007). The direct-FP-writer test does not scan this pool.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC: ActorEngine.grantBonusForcePoints / expireBonusForcePoints + spendForcePoints; ForcePointsService pool normalizer; one storage path.
findings.proposedSolution: Add one pool module (normalize/build) and ActorEngine grant/expire APIs; migrate the five builders; add a migration merging the foundryvtt-swse copy into flags.swse (or the reverse, decided once); extend the writer guard to bonusForcePoints.
findings.regressionTests: Guard test over bonusForcePoints writers; shim test for scope coherence after setFlag('swse').
findings.foundryAcceptance: Force Flow natural 1 grant, spend, end encounter; Guardian Spirit claim + spend + reload.
findings.coordinatorVerified: Same mechanism as F-TAL-007 (shared root cause).

findings.title: Guardian Spirit bonus FP pool in a different flag scope than the pool ActorEngine debits
findings.observed: GuardianSpiritActions writes actor.setFlag('swse','bonusForcePoints'), which SWSEActorBase.setFlag redirects to flags['foundryvtt-swse']. Every other writer (ActorEngine.spendForcePoints debit, Force Flow, force-adept, jedi-prestige, feats) writes the literal path flags.swse.bonusForcePoints. getFlag('swse') returns the foundryvtt-swse value first. After any Guardian Spirit claim or manual sheet adjustment, reads return the foundryvtt-swse pool: ActorEngine debits are written to flags.swse and never seen again (bonus points re-spendable) and later grants from other sources are hidden. spendBonusForcePoints also debits without a V2 receipt, queue or round-limit check. No test covers guardian-spirit-actions.js.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC: one bonus-pool API in ActorEngine/ForcePointsService (grant, expire, spend via spendForcePoints), one storage path.
findings.proposedSolution: Route GuardianSpirit grant/adjust through a single ActorEngine bonus-pool grant API writing the same path as spendForcePoints; route negative manual adjustment through an explicit MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT path; add a migration that merges any flags[foundryvtt-swse].bonusForcePoints into the canonical path. Extend the direct-FP-writer guard to the bonus pool.
findings.alternatives: Change all writers to setFlag('swse') consistently (still leaves the spend bypass).
findings.regressionTests: Shim test: claim Guardian Spirit, spend via ActorEngine.spendForcePoints, assert pool decremented and getFlag returns the decremented pool.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Guardian Spirit claim then FP spend, reload, check pool and ledger.
findings.risk: Existing worlds may already hold two copies; needs migration
findings.coordinatorVerified: SWSEActorBase.setFlag redirects scope swse -> foundryvtt-swse (swse-actor-base.js:463-465); getFlag prefers it (:447-451); ActorEngine debits literal flags.swse.bonusForcePoints (actor-engine.js:2127,2175). Precondition: a Guardian Spirit/sheet write of the pool.

findings.title: House-rule damage threshold computed independently by DerivedCalculator and ThresholdEngine with different formulas
findings.observed: RAW mode: ThresholdEngine reads system.derived.damageThreshold (single authority). With enableEnhancedMassiveDamage+modifyDamageThresholdFormula, DerivedCalculator stores base(incl. size, feat Will-base, flat/modifier adjustments)+level+size again, while ThresholdEngine.calculateDamageThreshold (used by evaluateThreshold on the live ActorEngine.applyDamage path) returns fort+level+size, ignoring the adjustments. Displayed DT and the DT used for the CT check differ under the house rule.
findings.intendedOwnership: DerivedCalculator owns DT (A-03); ThresholdEngine reads it.
findings.proposedSolution: After the owner rules on the house-rule formula, compute it once in DerivedCalculator and have calculateDamageThreshold always read system.derived.damageThreshold.
findings.alternatives: ThresholdEngine owns the house-rule formula and DerivedCalculator calls it.
findings.regressionTests: With the house rule on, derived DT === ThresholdEngine DT for character/droid/vehicle fixtures.
findings.foundryAcceptance: House rule enabled live; sheet DT equals applied threshold.
findings.risk: Changes house-rule outcomes — needs ruling first.

findings.title: Force Point maximum computed by two formulas; dailyForcePoints house rule never applied
findings.observed: Progression writes system.forcePoints.max from calculateMaxForcePointsForBuildPlan = base + floor(level/2) + MetaResourceFeatResolver bonus. ForcePointsService.getMax additionally applies the dailyForcePoints band and max(MetaResource, ForcePointFeatRules) bonus, but has no callers. ActorEngine.gainForcePoints caps at the stored max. Result: the registered dailyForcePoints house rule does not change the maximum; two feat-bonus readers exist.
findings.intendedOwnership: One FRC formula (ForcePointsService) consumed by progression.
findings.proposedSolution: Make calculateMaxForcePointsForBuildPlan delegate to a ForcePointsService build-plan entry point (same inputs) and delete the duplicate; owner confirms whether daily FP mode should drive the stored max.
findings.alternatives: Delete ForcePointsService.getMax and the house rule if daily mode is not wanted.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test: both entry points equal for the same build plan, with the house rule on and off.
findings.risk: Changes stored max for worlds using the house rule

findings.title: Trade/payout rollback is a parallel atomicity engine using whole-actor overwrite and item delete-and-recreate
findings.observed: When a multi-actor trade or job payout fails, Holonet restores each actor from a pre-operation toObject snapshot. It overwrites name, img, system, flags, ownership and prototypeToken (with skipValidation), deletes all current items and recreates them from the snapshot through ActorEngine.createEmbeddedDocuments with no keepId option. Effects get the same treatment. Results: (a) item and effect ids are expected to change, breaking id references such as equipped slots or upgrade links (Foundry default behavior, FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED); (b) any concurrent change to those actors (HP, conditions, other transactions) is silently reverted; (c) restore success is not verified (CR-HOL-02). This duplicates the exact-snapshot transactional rollback already in ActorEngine.applyMutationPlan / TransactionEngine (TI4-C0 G06-S1). Only the rollback path is affected; the success path is not.
findings.intendedOwnership: OSI / A-10: TransactionEngine owns atomic trades (credits, item transfer, approval, rollback).
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision. (a) Move multi-actor trade/payout settlement into a TransactionEngine operation (e.g. extend executeMutationTransaction to multi-actor plans) that uses targeted inverse operations and exact verification. (b) Minimum fix: restore only the fields and items the operation touched, use keepId:true, and verify the result.
findings.alternatives: Keep the current behavior and document it as a known L3 limitation (not recommended).
findings.regressionTests: Test: forced failure mid-trade; assert item ids unchanged and unrelated actor fields untouched after rollback.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Force a counter-offer failure between two owned actors; inspect item ids and equipped state.
findings.risk: High; credit movement and item identity.

findings.title: Three follower defense computations disagree; one installed by monkey-patching DefenseCalculator
findings.observed: The hotfix wraps DefenseCalculator.calculate for followers and rebuilds Fortitude with CON; the NPC sheet helper independently computes Fortitude as 10 + level + max(STR, CON) for display; the deriver applies template bonuses. A follower with STR > CON can show a different Fortitude than the one used by derived/rolls.
findings.intendedOwnership: DefenseCalculator (actor-core) computes follower defenses from a follower rules profile; the sheet displays derived values.
findings.proposedSolution: Defer the Fortitude ability rule to the owner (cite Galaxy at War follower rules); then implement once in DefenseCalculator via a follower profile (no prototype patch) and make npc-sheet-helpers read derived.defenses only.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Test: follower with STR 16 / CON 10 shows and rolls the same Fortitude.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: follower sheet defenses vs attack resolution.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One defense truth; one monkey-patch removed.
findings.risk: Wrong mechanics on a live path until resolved.

findings.title: Nonheroic class defined twice with divergent class skills
findings.observed: class-data-loader builds its own Nonheroic model (same BAB table and feat cadence, hitDie 4) with classSkills: [] and always seeds it into its cache; nonheroic-class-model.js defines NONHEROIC_CLASS_SKILLS (including the disputed ride). Consumers of getClassData see no Nonheroic class skills; ClassesRegistry consumers see the list.
findings.intendedOwnership: nonheroic-class-model.js as the only definition
findings.proposedSolution: class-data-loader returns adaptClassForLoaderCompatibility(createNonheroicClassModel()) instead of its own literal. The content of the skill list stays as is pending SWSE-NPC-RD-002.
findings.regressionTests: Test that getClassData("nonheroic") and ClassesRegistry Nonheroic agree on hitDie, BAB, classSkills, feat cadence
findings.risk: Low (exposes class skills to derived consumers; verify no consumer relied on empty list)

findings.title: Parallel class loader and cache bypassing ClassesDB
findings.observed: getClassData serves actor-core derived calculators from its own Map cache, sourced from ClassesRegistry when initialized, otherwise directly from the pack index with a separate normalize/adapt step. Two caches of the same compendium with separate invalidation.
findings.intendedOwnership: ClassesRegistry (ClassesDB) single cache; loader is a pure shape adapter
findings.proposedSolution: Make getClassData await ClassesRegistry.initialize() and adapt; delete the pack-index fallback and the separate cache once boot ordering guarantees registry readiness before first prepare.
findings.alternatives: Keep fallback but share the registry cache
findings.regressionTests: tests/class-hit-die-defense-source.test.mjs plus loader/registry equivalence test
findings.foundryAcceptance: Actor prepare before registries ready (world load)

findings.title: SWSERoll.rollAutofire / rollFullAttack keep independent defense, crit-range and crit-multiplier math; no in-repo caller
findings.observed: These entry points read target.system.defenses.reflex.total ?? 10 (no derived defense, Command Cover or observation bonus), use getEffectiveCritRange (EXTEND_CRITICAL_RANGE) instead of CombatOptionResolver criticalThreatNaturalMin, and combat-utils.getCriticalMultiplier (no criticalMultiplierMin). Canonical rollAttack uses getTargetDefense + resolveCriticalMultiplier. No static caller of rollAutofire/rollFullAttack except a hotfix that wraps rollAutofire; SWSERoll is not a global (macro use unverified). getDefenseValue/resolveTargetContext (:104/:116) and getWeaponDamageFormula (:55) are uncalled locals.
findings.intendedOwnership: combat-roll-math + attacks.js (C-CMB-2).
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the two methods and uncalled locals, or make them delegate to rollAttack / FullAttackExecutor (legacy B pending macro check).
findings.regressionTests: Guard: no second getCriticalMultiplier/defense reader in roll entry points.

findings.title: Two live installed-upgrade representations; inconsistent removal refunds
findings.observed: UpgradeService writes system.installedUpgrades (paid via TE; removal writes without refund); workbench writes flags.swse.*Upgrades/gearMods and flags.foundryvtt-swse.customization via TE. Readers of one do not see the other (TX-02, still open). Droid removal refunds resale through DroidCustomizationEngine.
findings.intendedOwnership: One installed-upgrade SSOT (A-01); V2 installer gated by TX-14.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner: choose SSOT (customization flag model) and route UpgradeService through the workbench plan builder; separately rule on removal refunds.
findings.alternatives: Mirror both until V2 installer certification.
findings.regressionTests: Install via either path visible to both readers.

findings.title: PrerequisiteChecker computes total level and BAB locally
findings.observed: getTotalLevel returns system.level ?? 1; getBaseAttackBonus returns the max of 12 stored/derived candidate paths (system.bab.*, system.derived.bab.*, system.combat.bab.*) and a value computed from class state. A stale stored value larger than the derived BAB wins (max), so a prerequisite can pass on stale data. Used at 4 call sites.
findings.intendedOwnership: Level from actor-core level-split; BAB from derived state (actor-core) or, for draft actors, from progression draft state passed explicitly.
findings.proposedSolution: Read BAB from system.derived.bab (single path) for committed actors and from the pending/draft projection for drafts; read level via level-split getTotalLevel. Keep the draft fallback behaviour behind an explicit "draft" input.
findings.regressionTests: Prereq tests with stale system.bab > derived.bab must fail the check; draft actor tests unchanged.

findings.title: Two droid readiness validators disagree on armor
findings.observed: DroidValidationEngine (sheet readiness and issues list) requires locomotion, >=1 appendage, processor and armor; the chargen droid builder requires locomotion, processor, >=1 appendage and resolved quotes but not armor; reconciliation notes the Store path does not require armor. A droid built legally in chargen/store shows 'not ready' on its sheet.
findings.intendedOwnership: One droid construction validator owned by the droid domain, used by builder, store and sheet.
findings.proposedSolution: Defer the rule (armor/appendage requirement) to the owner with source citation; then make one validator (pure, in scripts/domain/droids/) consumed by all three paths. Until ruled, the sheet should not claim 'not ready' for a missing armor component.
findings.alternatives: Keep both but label sheet readiness as advisory.
findings.regressionTests: Parity test: same droidSystems give the same verdict from builder and sheet.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: chargen droid without armor; sheet readiness.

findings.title: Second droid part overlay with hand-synced aliases and a divergent dead self-destruct export
findings.observed: The domain overlay keeps its own DROID_PART_CATEGORIES, alias table and getDroidPartDefinition/getSelfDestructDamage; only resolveDroidSystemIdentity/actorMeetsDroidSystemRequirement are consumed (prerequisite-checker). Its getSelfDestructDamage disagrees with the canonical table for miniaturized systems but has no consumer.
findings.intendedOwnership: scripts/data/droid-part-schema.js is the only part-definition authority; prerequisite identity resolves through it.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the unused exports (getSelfDestructDamage, getDroidPartDefinition, DROID_PART_CATEGORIES) from the domain overlay now (class C); then reimplement resolveDroidSystemIdentity on the canonical normalizeDroidPartId + alias table and retire the overlay.
findings.alternatives: Generate the alias table from the canonical file.
findings.regressionTests: Prerequisite tests for 'requires Heuristic Processor' etc. pass against canonical ids; test that no module imports getSelfDestructDamage from the domain file.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Feat/talent prerequisite checks on a droid.

findings.title: Normalization hooks hard-code a second copy of feat rules diverging from canonical abilityMeta
findings.observed: rulesForFeat(name) tables in each family define runtime rule objects by feat name. For Confident Success the canonical record carries skillSuccessResourceRules type GRANT_FORCE_POINT_ON_SUCCESS; the hook writes resourceRules.forcePoints type GAIN_NORMAL_FP_ON_SKILL_APPLICATION_SUCCESS, which is what force-point-feat-actions reads (with a name fallback). The canonical rule is unread.
findings.intendedOwnership: data/canonical/feats.json (R-FEA-01) is the single rule source; runtime reads one shape.
findings.proposedSolution: Per family, move the rule objects into the canonical record (owner-approved data change through tools/build-feat-production.mjs) and delete the hook table; until then add a CI check that flags feats whose canonical abilityMeta rule types are not consumed.
findings.alternatives: Declare the hook tables authoritative and strip unused rule shapes from canonical data (requires owner decision since it contradicts Phase 5C).
findings.regressionTests: Census-style test: every abilityMeta rule type in canonical feats has a runtime consumer, and no rulesForFeat table exists for a migrated family.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Confident Success grant works on a feat created from the pack without normalization.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes ~18 name-keyed rule tables and runtime writes
findings.risk: Data migration of existing actor-owned feat items

findings.title: Dark Side Score mutation has no owner (7 live writer modules)
findings.observed: DSPEngine is pure; each caller composes the new value and writes system.darkSide.value via ActorEngine.updateActor. Logging differs (force-engine pushes into actor.system.dspLog in place before update; force-adept logs before/after/delta; sith logs reason only; temptation/poison/alchemy none). poison-engine uses getValue()+n instead of getNextValue. Orphan force-suite.js and utils/force-points.js add two more.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC: one DSS mutation (ActorEngine.adjustDarkSideScore(actor, delta, reason) computing via DSPEngine).
findings.proposedSolution: Add the API and migrate the 7 writers; keep DSPEngine pure.
findings.regressionTests: Guard listing allowed system.darkSide.value writers; dsp-engine-behavior extension.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Dark side power use, Temptation, poison DSS increase.

findings.title: Ability modifier and skill reading reimplemented across suggestion modules
findings.observed: Canonical SchemaAdapters.getAbilityMod exists. Suggestion modules each read different paths (system.attributes.<k>.mod, system.abilities.<k>.mod, total/value/score fallbacks) and recompute floor((score-10)/2) locally; shared-suggestion-utilities already uses SchemaAdapters for scores but recomputes the modifier, ignoring derived modifiers. Different fallback orders can give different advisory results for the same actor. The formula itself is standard; this is a schema-interpretation duplicate, not a rules question.
findings.intendedOwnership: Derived ability modifiers: actor-core / SchemaAdapters (A-03).
findings.proposedSolution: Replace every local reader with SchemaAdapters.getAbilityMod/getAbilityScore; make extractAbilityModifiers delegate.
findings.alternatives: One suggestion-local adapter that delegates to SchemaAdapters.
findings.regressionTests: Extend tests/consumer-batch-ability-authority.test.mjs with a source guard forbidding '(score - 10) / 2' in scripts/engine/suggestion.
findings.risk: Advisory rankings may shift slightly where fallbacks differed.

findings.title: Three independent BAB calculations in progression with divergent behavior on sparse class tables
findings.observed: levelup-shared.calculateTotalBAB matches lp.level === classLevel exactly; class-suggestion-utilities.calculateTotalBAB uses the highest row <= classLevel and accepts more field spellings; progression-data.calculateBAB indexes level_progression[level-1] from class-data-loader. The Summary step preview uses the old-app helper. actor-prerequisite-snapshot calculateBab reads prepared actor values (consumer, not duplicate).
findings.intendedOwnership: actor-core derived calculator (A-03) or a single class-table BAB function in classes domain.
findings.proposedSolution: Choose one class-table BAB function (classes domain), make the other two delegate, and have previews read it.
findings.regressionTests: Table test over all class records comparing the three outputs (should be identical for complete tables).

findings.title: Local skill-total formulas in the rolls domain
findings.observed: getSkillTotal returns a locally rebuilt component total (ability + half level + trained + focus + misc) for useTheForce, and otherwise prefers derived totals with a component fallback. calculateCustomSkillBonus computes ability + 5 trained + 5 focus + floor(system.level/2) + misc. skills.calculateSkillModifier (exported, no importer) omits half level entirely. The derived skill pipeline (actor-core/ABL) is the authority for normal skills.
findings.intendedOwnership: Skill totals from the derived skill pipeline; dialogs display the derived total and its breakdown.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete calculateSkillModifier (dead). Make the UTF dialog base read the derived UTF total plus an explicit breakdown (the comment says duplicate passive effects were the reason; fix duplication in the derived pipeline instead - see F-ACT-015). Custom skills: compute in the derived pipeline; the half-level source is a deferred rules question (deferredRules).
findings.regressionTests: Parity tests: dialog base == derived total for every skill incl. UTF; custom skill fixtures.

findings.title: Local Dark Side Score increment helpers in force-adept and sith actions
findings.observed: Each computes DSPEngine.getNextValue and writes system.darkSide.value plus a differently shaped dspLog entry via ActorEngine.updateActor. DSPEngine has no mutation API. See F-FRC-004 for the full writer set.
findings.intendedOwnership: FRC Dark Side Score mutation API.
findings.proposedSolution: Use the FRC DSS API proposed in F-FRC-004.
findings.regressionTests: dsp-engine-behavior extended.

findings.title: Presentation recomputes Second Wind and defense values
findings.observed: buildSecondWindPanel computes max(floor(HP/4), CON) with its own CON fallback and max uses default 1, ignoring SecondWindRules healing modes, multipliers, feat rules and house-rule use counts. The defense tooltip rebuilds a subtotal and uses it as the total when derived total is falsy, and selects Fort ability by actor type.
findings.intendedOwnership: SecondWindRules / DefenseCalculator compute; panels display derived values.
findings.proposedSolution: Expose SecondWindRules.calculateHealingAmount/calculateMaxUses results in derived data (or call them from the builder); tooltip shows derived total and breakdown terms only, with 'unavailable' when absent.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Test with secondWindWebEnhancement house rule: panel shows engine values.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Second Wind panel with house rules toggled.

findings.title: Second prerequisite evaluator in the item dialog
findings.observed: The entity dialog evaluates ability/BAB/level/class/feat/talent clauses with its own evaluator; progression uses prerequisite-evaluator.js. Both live; results can disagree.
findings.intendedOwnership: Progression prerequisite authority evaluates; dialog displays.
findings.proposedSolution: Have the dialog call the progression evaluator (adapter for its clause shape); keep normalizePrereqClauses as the editor normalizer only.
findings.alternatives: none
findings.regressionTests: Parity test: same clauses/actor give the same met/unmet in both.

findings.title: Two spend paths for starship maneuvers with different semantics
findings.observed: Vehicle sheet useManeuver writes system.discarded=true on the crew/vehicle item without a roll; the character sheet uses StarshipManeuverSuite.activateManeuver (Pilot activation check, then discarded). Regain on the vehicle sheet already delegates to the suite.
findings.intendedOwnership: StarshipManeuverSuite is the single maneuver use/regain authority; vehicle sheet is a view/adapter.
findings.proposedSolution: Route vehicle-sheet use through StarshipManeuverSuite.activateManeuver(pilot,itemId); keep StarshipManeuversEngine as list builder only. If a manual 'mark spent' GM tool is wanted, owner must say so.
findings.alternatives: Keep manual toggle as GM-only override with explicit label.
findings.regressionTests: Test that vehicle-sheet use invokes the suite and produces a Pilot activation roll.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Live V13: use maneuver from vehicle Pilot station.
findings.risk: Low; behavior change visible to players.

findings.title: Dual flag scope: setFlag("swse") is remapped to "foundryvtt-swse" while most reads use flags.swse
findings.observed: SWSEActorBase.setFlag/unsetFlag rewrite scope "swse" to the system id; getFlag("swse") reads foundryvtt-swse then falls back to flags.swse. Code that writes via actor.update({"flags.swse.x"}) persists to flags.swse, while ActorEngine.updateActorFlags(actor,"swse",...) persists to flags["foundryvtt-swse"]. git grep counts ~1,535 flags.swse references vs ~182 flags["foundryvtt-swse"]. Direct property reads of flags.swse.x miss values written through setFlag("swse"). Not traced per key.
findings.intendedOwnership: One canonical flag namespace with one accessor.
findings.proposedSolution: Inventory keys written through each path (census of setFlag scope + flags.swse writes) and pick one namespace; until then, require ActorEngine flag helpers and getFlag for reads. Owner decision on the canonical scope.
findings.regressionTests: Per-key round-trip tests write via each path and read via each accessor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Verify setFlag("swse") persistence location in Foundry v13.
findings.risk: Migration of persisted flags is a runtime-risk area.

findings.title: Generic utilities compute game rules
findings.observed: math-utils defines calculateBAB/calculateDefense/calculateDamageThreshold/calculateCarryingCapacity; SchemaAdapters.getAbilityMod/getDefense/getBAB/getConditionPenalty read derived values and fall back to their own formulas. Consumers of math-utils were not traced per call site.
findings.intendedOwnership: Rule formulas in actor-core/combat; utils only read derived.
findings.proposedSolution: Trace math-utils consumers; delete unused functions; make SchemaAdapters fall back to null/unknown (A-12 "unknown is not false") instead of recomputing, or to the actor-core helper.
findings.regressionTests: schema-adapters-ability-authority test extended to fallbacks.

findings.title: DerivedOverrideEngine computes HALF_LEVEL and ability mod independently of actor-core helpers
findings.observed: _getHalfLevel uses floor(system.level/2); level-split provides getHeroicHalfLevel/getEffectiveHalfLevel. _getAbilityMod recomputes from attributes as fallback. HALF_LEVEL is referenced only by orphan phase-3-feat-definitions.js and the contract, so no live feature uses it.
findings.intendedOwnership: Level and ability-mod arithmetic from one owner (actor-core level-split, derived attributes).
findings.proposedSolution: Delegate _getAbilityMod to derived attributes only and leave HALF_LEVEL unimplemented (throw/deny) until a feature needs it; which level (heroic vs character) a generic HALF_LEVEL means is a rules question to raise at that time.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test for ABILITY_MOD override.

findings.title: Condition-track penalty table duplicated in four modules
findings.observed: Identical literal [0,-1,-2,-5,-10,0] in four places; defense-calculator prefers derived.damage.conditionPenalty and falls back to its own copy. Values agree today.
findings.intendedOwnership: One condition-track rule owner (combat ConditionTrackRules) consumed by actor-core.
findings.proposedSolution: Expose the table from ConditionTrackRules (or a pure constants module) and import it at the four sites. No value changes.
findings.regressionTests: Golden defense lifecycle test plus a unit test asserting all consumers read one table.

findings.title: CombatEngine.applyDamage is a second, incomplete damage writer with no caller
findings.observed: Calls DamageResolutionEngine.resolveDamage then writes only system.hp.value and conditionTrack.current via ActorEngine.updateActor (no bonus/temp HP, shields, persistent CT, droid states, FP-rescue receipt that ActorEngine.applyDamage handles). No static caller, not in packs, CombatEngine not global.
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine.applyDamage sole damage boundary.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the method or make it delegate to ActorEngine.applyDamage (legacy C/D).
findings.regressionTests: architecture-combat-authority guard: no second resolveDamage caller.

findings.title: Dead carrying-capacity rule in progression EquipmentEngine
findings.observed: getCarryingCapacity = Str x 10 (no size) and isOverEncumbered have no caller; EncumbranceEngine uses math-utils.calculateCarryingCapacity with size.
findings.intendedOwnership: EncumbranceEngine
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the two methods (progression domain owner).
findings.regressionTests: n/a

findings.title: Settings defined twice with divergent definitions
findings.observed: darkSideMaxMultiplier, allowSuiteReselection, store.requireGMApproval, pendingCustomPurchases are registered in settings.js and again in houserule-settings.js (skipped at runtime by its has() guard, so the houserule-settings definitions are dead and differ, e.g. darkSideMaxMultiplier range). themePromptShown is registered in settings.js and ui-manager.js with different name/hint.
findings.intendedOwnership: One definition per setting key; house-rule keys defined in the HRL manifest.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the duplicates in settings.js for house-rule keys (keep HRL as owner) or vice versa per owner; keep one themePromptShown. Add a test that every key is registered exactly once.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test registering all settings into a fake registry asserting no duplicate keys.
findings.risk: Low; definitions must be merged carefully (range/choices).

findings.title: Second isEpicOverrideEnabled reads game.settings directly
findings.observed: level-split.js defines its own isEpicOverrideEnabled via game.settings.get; settings/epic-override.js exports one via HouseRuleService.isEnabled.
findings.intendedOwnership: One accessor via HouseRuleService (A-06).
findings.proposedSolution: Re-export the settings accessor from level-split (or import it) and delete the local copy.
findings.regressionTests: Unit: both paths return the same value under fake settings.

findings.title: House-rule defaults declared in three places
findings.observed: Sampled keys agree (e.g. criticalHitVariant default standard in all three); no test enforces parity across the three.
findings.intendedOwnership: One declaration from which registration, defaults and manifest derive.
findings.proposedSolution: Generate registration + defaults from the manifest (or add a parity test first).
findings.regressionTests: Parity test over all keys.

findings.title: Normal Force Point balance spend/regain: single authority confirmed; lead not a duplicate
findings.observed: Spend: ForceEngine.spendForcePoint delegates to ActorEngine.spendForcePoints + finalize (wrapper, legacy D-style but thin and typed). Regain: ActorEngine.gainForcePoints uses ForcePointsService.calcGain (pure). ForcePointsService.calcSpend has no callers (dead helper). scripts/utils/force-points.js (ForcePointsUtil) is orphan. Talent-side debit exists only for the bonus pool (F-FRC-003).
findings.intendedOwnership: ActorEngine mutation + ForcePointsService calculation (as observed).
findings.proposedSolution: Delete calcSpend and the orphan util after owner confirmation; keep ForceEngine.spendForcePoint or inline it at its 3 call sites.
findings.regressionTests: existing direct-fp-writer guard

findings.title: Mechanical-responsibility leads are delegations, not duplicates
findings.observed: Condition steps delegate to ConditionTrackRules/ConditionEngine; getAbilityMod reads the prepared mod first; normalizeAbilityMods normalizes data shape; rage attack/damage bonus is a distinct species mechanic.
findings.proposedSolution: None
